Motion. Time to set in motion.

Leonard pondered the thought vomit that coursed through his mind, catching brief glimpses along the way. He lingered on the fond memories of his past as he looked over the rusty dunes and into the stars of the night, knowing the Pale Blue Dot was among them. His favorite bar came to mind; the place of comfort where he had met the stranger that skyrocketed him onto the path that he walked now. Well, the path that led him to hiding in the foliage he currently huddled under at least. He was waiting to take the next step on his course.

Waiting, waiting to strike, Strike, STRIKE! Soon, soon time to set in motion

He visibly flinched as he heard the rustling in the bushes behind him, despite knowing what was making the noises. Leonard had developed the ability to see the immediate future with absolute certainty thanks to his modifications, but he still took comfort in reacting as a human should in certain situations. Another deluge of thoughts washed over him about what it really meant to be human as a creature not unlike a Lynx sauntered out of the brush and over to Leonard.

"You're getting distracted again, do not forget our mission tonight" The Lynx spoke in a deep, somewhat gravelly voice. While it's appearance reflected that of an earthling creature, no part of it ever came from that planet. It was organic in design, but built from the ground up like any mechanical contraption. Leonard pushed the thoughts away, since thinking about the mechanical organism was only going to draw him further into his own mind.

"No, I haven't forgotten. Just adjusting to the enhancements still" he muttered. "Still waiting for the sign for us to..." he trailed off as a humanoid robot crossed into his line of sight. No, not a robot. That one actually was a human, merely clad in a mechanical suit designed to protect the human within from any attempts to kill or maim it. He smiled to himself, knowing the inevitable fate of the human within, as his left hand materialized into a serrated blade, thin and sharp, yet stronger than any material known to it's future victim. Leonard stood and approached the man, knowing the human wouldn't be able to see him or his impending doom. This would make it easier for Leonard to do his job without resistance and make the most efficient strike for the sake of his victim. He grasped the man's head with his right hand and inserted the bladed hand into the base of his skull, severing the spine from the rest of the organic system, and produced a shrill frequency from his right hand, melting the control system (or brain as he would have once called it) with the other. The human crumpled without making a sound, and Leonard continued on his predetermined path.

He looked to the sky for the next step in his plan, ignoring the spotlights searching the open swath of land, where the incoming ships would expect to land and release it's cargo. The lights shifted over the field and eventually focused on the deceased body of the human that Leonard had eliminated. A flashing red light and a wailing siren sounded accompanied the discovery, and more humans filed out of the tall structure that the spotlight was attached to. As they sprinted towards the dead human with their weapons drawn, one by one they slammed to the ground under some invisible weight. Leonard knew it was the Lynx that was dropping them, but was unable to see it. He turned to the sky to find 3 flickering lights moving across the sky with increasing speed. Suddenly the lights and sirens stopped, but Leonard was too fixated on the sky, as the lights were growing in size. The lights were starting to transition into 3 ships that were making their descents towards the surface of the planet when the Lynx approached him again.

"You forgot to hide the body, Leonard. Those men were killed because of your negligence" the Lynx growled at Leonard. The disapproving tone in the creature's voice only made Leonard chuckle.

"If they didn't die today, then they would have been eliminated in the not so distant future. Better to end them now than to let them suffer their existence" Leonard retorted, refusing to break away from the inbound ships.

"You feel for these beings, as if you are still one of them. You will need to address that before you are ready for your destiny" the Lynx remarked, as it too turned it's gaze towards the sky. Leonard grunted in response, neither confirming nor denying the statement. He raised his left arm, now in the shape of some firearm, and pointed it at the ships. An orange glow and a low hum started to emanate from the weapon as it powered up, and once it was ready, a blindingly white light shot out at the lead ship. In a brilliant burst in the sky, the ship exploded and sent a shockwave out that collided with the following ships. The ship closest to the explosion listed off course, as debris started to drop off the hull. The third was hit with the shockwave as well, but it appeared to be heading straight for the landing site where Leonard and the Lynx were standing.

"You have no qualms with ending the humans on this planet, and yet you leave a ship infested with them to crash onto our surface? Perhaps I miscalculated your medal when choosing you for this mission" the Lynx stated, which only annoyed Leonard.

"No, we need them to understand they aren't welcome here. If it's perceived as a malfunction, then they will try it again" Leonard replied. "Someone needs to live to regret their actions and to deter a further invasion." This seemed to satisfy the cat's inquiry, but Leonard knew the silence was only temporary.

"Then we need to head on to the target. She will be waiting for us" the creature replied, turning towards the second ship. It appeared to be heading into the heart of the forest, and the lynx started in that direction. Leonard paused for a moment as his thoughts took hold of his consciousness. He shook himself free of their hold, and a solemn look came over his face.

Set in motion. All set in motion

"And so it begins..." he muttered, and sprinted off after his accomplice and towards the immanent crash site.
